title: Emirate of Bukhara
capsule: The Emirate of Bukhara was a Manghit Uzbek state in Transoxiana, founded by Muhammad Rahim (r. 1753–1758), who transformed the nominally Chinggisid khanate of Bukhara into a dynasty ruling in its own name. The emirate controlled the Zerafshan valley and major trade centres including Bukhara and Samarkand, functioning as a nominally independent buffer state after becoming a Russian protectorate under the Treaty of 1868 following Emir Muzaffar al-Din's defeat at Jizzakh. Emir Alim Khan (r. 1910–1920) was overthrown when the Red Army under Mikhail Frunze took Bukhara by storm in September 1920, dissolving the emirate and replacing it with the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The emirate's core territory is well attested from Russian imperial surveys and treaty maps; peripheral dependencies in the Pamirs and eastern Bukhara are less precisely delimited.
